newsitem.title: UK: Lomond Underwriting sets first day premium.
newsitem.headline: Lomond Underwriting sets first day premium.

text.p: Shares in Lomond Underwriting Plc, a Lloyd's corporate vehicle formed by fund manager Murray Johnstone in 1993, set a five percent premium on their first day of trading on the London Stock Exchange on Thursday.
The shares were quoted at 128-1/2p by 1300 GMT, a 6p premium to the price in the company's recent placing. Trading volume reached 221,400 shares.
"The listing of Lomond marks a further significant step in the company's development," said chairman Sir Raymond Johnstone.
"The increased share capital and reinsurance arrangements have allowed us to acquire some attractive capacity at what is seen as an opportune time," he added.
The company raised 11.7 million stg in a private placing through UBS Ltd, which acted as sponsor, with institutions taking most of the shares.
The placing, which followed a 1993 issue raising 28.7 million stg, valued Lomond at about 40 million stg.
